evidence_method: Classify explicitly described YouTube channel-monetization examples by creative contribution and cross-check separate copyright/fair-use/Content ID rules. Cases are generic hypotheticals, not sampled uploads.

published_example_cases.title: Reaction with substantive spoken analysis
published_example_cases.example_notes: Critical commentary that changes the viewer's experience is described as potentially monetizable.

published_example_cases.title: Sports replay with explained competitor moves
published_example_cases.example_notes: YouTube gives analytical sports commentary as a platform originality example; event footage may be protected.

published_example_cases.title: Movie scene with rewritten dialogue and voiceover
published_example_cases.example_notes: Substantive transformation is an example under reused-content review; legal rights remain independent.

published_example_cases.title: Silent/mostly nonverbal reaction with minimal commentary
published_example_cases.example_notes: YouTube identifies primarily nonverbal reactions as a disallowed reused-content example.

published_example_cases.title: Short clips collected from other social websites
published_example_cases.example_notes: Simple compilations without distinct commentary or new narrative are identified as ineligible examples.

published_example_cases.title: Collection of licensed songs by unrelated artists
published_example_cases.example_notes: YouTube lists collections of different artists' songs as disallowed, even when permission is given.

published_example_cases.title: Third-party footage edited with clear new storyline and commentary
published_example_cases.example_notes: YouTube treats substantial creator storytelling and editing as a potentially acceptable reused-content example.

jurisdiction_note: US fair use is one copyright exception; fair dealing and other exceptions have different local conditions. Platform originality review is not a copyright ruling.
